label: Can fail to be; corruptible in a respect: CanFailToBe x r: x can fail to be r
term: can fail to be (contingit non esse); corruptible in a respect
definition: `CanFailToBe x r`: x can fail to be r. Aquinas identifies what can fail to be with the corruptible, simply when r is substance and in a respect (secundum quid) when r is a place, quantity or quality: a body that can fail to be in a place is corruptible in place (In Metaph. IX, lect. 9 n. 4). The case reads it in the two-way sense of the potency of the contradictory: what is in potency to r is possible to be r and possible not to be r (possibile esse et non esse, lect. 9 n. 2), not the bare possibility of not being r (DISAMB-CAN-FAIL-TO-BE-OR-BE-OTHERWISE). A Lean primitive: it is not defined from act or potency, and no modal semantics (possible worlds or times) is encoded, so the readings constrain it only through their stated implications.
